To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the medial pre-frontal cortex is required for recognition memory based on recency, and the prelimbic and infralimbilic regions of the medial pre-front cortex are involved in recognition memory based on object location.
Lesions to the PL and IL cortices disrupt recency and object location recognition memory, respectively, whereas novel object recognition is intact.
catecholamine depletion within the PL and IL cortices of the medial prefrontic cortex disrupt recognition memory for object recency and location, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the medial prefrontic cortex contributes to recognition memory.
the neural mechanisms underlying recognition memory.
the neural mechanisms that underlie the formation and retrieval of episodic memories in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mP FC is not required for discrimination based on the relative recency of two objects.
the PL is involved in the recency task and the IL is involved in the object location task.
these results suggest that the mPFOC is involved in different processes of recognition memory and the role of catecholaminergic system in these processes is not uniform across the PL and IL cortices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the catecholaminergic system within the mP FC is important for recognition memory for recency and location, but not identity.
the PL is critical for the processing of recency information, whereas the IL is important for integrating spatial and object information.
catecholaminergic depletion within the PL and IL cortices differentially affects recognition memory for recency, object locations, and objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the PL and IL cortices of the medial prefront cortex (mP FC) are involved in the processing of recency information and that the PL cortex may be involved in the processing and integration of location information.
the PL and IL subregions of the mPFC are differentially important for recency and location judgments.
the mP FC is not a homogeneous structure and the PL and IL cortices have distinct roles in recognition memory.
